messages:
maya_cs: Quick sync — I'm putting together a short, customer-facing SOP for proactive priming (tenant hydration), streaming fallbacks, and the telemetry hooks we should use to detect renewal risk. Looking for quick feedback before I turn this into a PDF + support playbook.

alex_sre: +1. Keep it prescriptive. Customers want a 3-step runbook more than a long essay. We should include the circuit-breaker and model-fallback thresholds. e.g. if p95 latency > 1s for 3m -> route to compact model. :thumbsup:

jamal_pm: Couple of PM asks: 1) a short blurb we can include in renewal emails about why priming helps (and cost transparency) 2) a rollback path that CS can call during noisy priming.

maya_cs: Draft outline I'm thinking: 1) Preflight checks (traffic forecast, target qps, region) 2) Priming run (what to prefill, TTL, parallelism + jitter) 3) Live ops (what to monitor, alerts, escalation) 4) Fallbacks (streaming degrade -> compact model -> queued batch) 5) Customer comms templates. Thoughts?

sara_eng: I'll drop a minimal prefill example and batching guidance — keep it runnable. Small tips: prefer staggered priming windows, RNG offsets to avoid thundering herd, and keep per-tenant priming work limited to ~15% of your peak QPS to avoid overshoot.

maya_cs: Example CLI we can hand to customers:
```bash
# prefill top prefixes for tenant T-123 (approx 500 keys)
redwood prefill --tenant T-123 --model rdx-small --prefill-keys keys.json --parallel 4 --ttl 3600
```
And a tiny curl fallback mapping we can recommend in their proxy config:
```json
{
  "route_policy": [
    {"when": "p95_latency>1000", "action": "route_to:rdx-small"},
    {"when": "queue_depth>50", "action": "batch_and_defer"}
  ]
}
```

alex_sre: Operational thresholds to include in the SOP (suggested):
- Priming window: prefer 30-90m before go-live (staggered across tenants)
- Priming concurrency: keep <15% of node capacity per tenant
- Circuit-breaker: p95_latency > 1000ms for 3 consecutive minutes OR error_rate > 3% -> trigger fallback route
- Cost guardrail: estimated token prefill budget must be approved if > $250/day

lia_cs: Renewal-signal telemetry (what CS will look at):
- sudden drop in DAU/usage (7-day moving avg drop > 20%)
- sustained latency increase (above thresholds)
- growing % of streamed responses that timeout or NACK
- negative sentiment in customer feedback tickets
Composite risk_score = weighted sum (usage_change, latency_change, error_rate, feedback_score). Escalate at risk_score >= 0.6.

jamal_pm: Nice. For customer comms, short template suggestion: "We're priming your account to improve response quality and keep latency low during launch. This may generate a one-time cost increase of ~$X. We'll notify you before starting and can pause on request." Keep it short.

maya_cs: Adding a rollback play: 1) pause priming job 2) clear primed keys for tenant (if corruption suspected) 3) flip route to fallback model 4) open a joint incident channel with eng-sre and product 5) offer to revert to pre-priming configuration.

ops-bot: Job queued: prefill-T-123 (job-id: pf-84f3) scheduled for 2026-04-01T02:00:00Z.

sara_eng: One more technical note to include: prefer prefix hashing for keys (top n prefixes) instead of full-doc prefill; it gives wide coverage with less token cost. Also throttle tokenization calls with a 50ms inter-request gap when priming at scale.

maya_cs: This is great — I'll consolidate into a 1-pager + a short customer-facing FAQ. If no objections, I'll publish the draft tomorrow and share the link here. :eyes:

alex_sre: No objections from SRE. Please include contact on-call rotation for escalation.

lia_cs: Will add the renewal escalation steps and sample datapoints we need from telemetry.

maya_cs: Thanks all — I'll ping when it's live.
